meta.title: Locrian, and When a Mode Collapses
meta.summary: Seven questions on the home chord that will not hold, what a tonic actually needs, why the notes that clash belong to the chord rather than the scale, and what happens the moment a progression arrives somewhere.

prompt.text: Which of these does a mode actually need? Select every one that applies.

spans.text: Something outside the scale holding one note as home — a drone, a bass, or a chord that will not move.
A home chord with a perfect fifth in it, so it is a chord you can stand on.
A characteristic note — the one tone the mode is named for.
A progression that resolves, so the ear is told where home is.

explanation.text: Those two are the definition, and it took until Locrian to see that the second one was missing from it. A characteristic note is not required: Ionian and Aeolian have none and are still modes. And a progression that resolves does the opposite of what a mode needs — it names its own tonic by arriving somewhere, which is exactly what a vamp refuses to do.
